descriptiontext: A topic area categorisation of the UK Measures of National Well-being, which people told us mattered to their well-being. The 10 domains are personal well-being, our relationships, health, what we do, where we live, personal finance, education and skills, economy, governance and environment.
Final energy consumption is the direct consumption of fuels compared to primary consumption that relates to the fuel input.

A measure of the overall extent to which groupings of households, from the bottom of the income distribution upwards, receive less than an equal share of income. For example, the bottom 5% of households might only have a 1% share of total household income. The lower its value, the more equally household income is distributed.

The total value of output in the economic territory. It is the balancing item on the production account for the whole economy. Domestic product can be measured as gross or net. It is presented in the accounts at market (or purchasers’) prices.

Healthy life expectancy (HLE) is defined as the number of years an individual can expect to spend in very good or good general health. It can either be calculated as years from birth or years remaining from a fixed point.
The knowledge, skills and characteristics embodied in individuals that facilitate the creation of personal, social and economic well-being.
How we represent and track the things people told us matter to their well-being within each of the 10 domains.

The median household income is the income of what would be the middle household, if all households in the UK were sorted in a list from poorest to richest. As it represents the middle of the income distribution, the median household income provides a good indication of the standard of living of the “typical” household in terms of income.
Focus on reporting facts about people’s lives and the spaces in which they live.

Change over time is presented as the difference in the unit of measurement from the most recent time point to the time point compared over the short term. For measures reported as a percentage estimate, the change in the estimate is presented as a percentage point change rather than percent change.
The period before Quarter 1 (January to March) 2020.

Net debt, for the purposes of UK fiscal policy, is defined as total gross financial liabilities less liquid financial assets, where liquid assets are cash and short-term assets, which can be realised for cash at short notice and without significant loss. These liquid assets mainly comprise foreign exchange reserves and bank deposits. The net debt is a cash measure that is priced at nominal value (the cost to the issuer at redemption) and consolidated (intra-sector holdings of liabilities/assets are removed).

The purpose of seasonal adjustment is to remove systematic calendar-related variation associated with the time of the year (seasonal effects). This facilitates comparisons between consecutive time periods.

Measures have been assessed as having improved or declined if the difference between the comparison periods is statistically significant using non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals, where available. If a difference is said to be statistically significant, it is unlikely that it could have occurred by chance alone.
More information on statistical significance and confidence intervals is available.
Focus on directly asking people about their feelings, opinions and sentiments.
Unpaid work includes unpaid household work (for example, cooking and cleaning), DIY, gardening, unpaid childcare, unpaid adult care and volunteering.
